channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Alaska Could Help Flip the Senate
item.description: Democrat Mary Peltola has a lot in the way of unseating Republican Senator Dan S. Sullivan for an Alaska Senate seat. Their race will offer clues about the fate of other red states this year, Bloomberg Opinion columnist Ronald Brownstein says. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ukraine Resumes Attacks on Oil Refineries Deep Inside Russia
item.description: Ukraine says it hit oil-processing plants in Russia’s Perm region and Tatarstan overnight, resuming attacks after US envoys visited Moscow this weekend.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: UK's Healey Vows Fiscal Rigor and to Boost Regional Growth
item.description: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey said he will build on his predecessor Rachel Reeves’ efforts to reestablish the UK’s credibility in international bond markets. Speaking in the Midlands city of Coventry, Healey also outlined plans to boost regional economies, cut legislation and double the number of so-called unicorn firms in Britain. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Europe Far-Right Shift Gives Russian Leader Putin a Lifeline
item.description: The AfD’s election victory in an eastern state shows its growing confidence in challenging the German establishment.
item.dc:creator: Anthony Halpin

item.title: German Far Right Surges in Vote, Iran & US Trade Tanker Attacks | The Opening Trade 9/7/2026
item.description:
The far-right Alternative for Germany scored its best-ever result in a state election on Sunday amid growing public discontent with the political establishment, delivering a powerful blow to Chancellor Friedrich Merz.
Iran and the US carried out what appeared to be their largest tit-for-tat tanker strikes yet over the weekend, pushing oil prices higher as both nations continue to escalate a six-month war that has disrupted shipping and stoked global inflation.
The Opening Trade has everything you need to know as markets open across Europe. With analysis you won't find anywhere else, we break down the biggest stories of the day and speak to top guests who have skin in the game. Hosted by Guy Johnson. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Russia, North Korea Finish First Road Bridge Link As Ties Deepen
item.description: North Korea and Russia held a ceremony to mark the completion of the first road bridge linking the two countries, in a fresh sign of deepening ties between Moscow and Kim Jong Un’s regime.
item.dc:creator: Soobin Kim

item.title: Merz Moves to Contain Fallout From Far-Right Rout in State Vote
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz is facing intensifying pressure to come up with a convincing response after an overwhelming victory by the far right in a state election delivered a powerful blow to the political establishment.
item.dc:creator: Arne Delfs, Kamil Kowalcze and Michael Nienaber

item.title: Fictitious Names Used in Secret Duterte Payments, Witness Says
item.description: Philippines Vice President Sara Duterte allegedly used names prosecutors say were fictitious or belonged to dead people, including children, to document intelligence-gathering state funds, her impeachment trial heard Monday.
item.dc:creator: Neil Jerome Morales

item.title: Pakistan Shows Possible China Missile System as Ties Deepen
item.description: Pakistan’s military showcased an air defense system in a promotional video that resembles a Chinese platform, potentially signaling another layer to defense cooperation that has deepened since the 2025 India-Pakistan conflict.
item.dc:creator: Josh Xiao and Tooba Khan

item.title: Chinese Chip Spy Suspect Arrested Before Brussels-Beijing Flight
item.description: A Chinese citizen suspected of spying on a Belgian semiconductor firm was arrested as he attempted to take a flight back to Beijing from Brussels earlier this year.
item.dc:creator: Max Ramsay

item.title: US Turns Diplomatic Screws on Iran for Atomic Non-Compliance
item.description: The US is increasing diplomatic pressure on Iran by proposing that Tehran be referred to the United Nations Security Council over its stonewalling of nuclear inspectors, who have been unable to verify the location of the country’s stockpile of near-weapons-grade uranium.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Tirone

item.title: Iran Says Strait of Hormuz Deal With Oman Just Days Away
item.description: Iran said a deal with Oman to manage shipping through the Strait of Hormuz is imminent, a move that could tighten Tehran’s control over the waterway and raise questions over how the US would respond.
item.dc:creator: Eltaf Najafizada and Alex Longley

item.title: Hanoi Seeks to Woo Red River Residents by Doubling Compensation
item.description: Vietnam’s capital has recommended doubling payments for residents forced from their homes for the controversial $28 billion Red River boulevard project, as Hanoi officials seek to reduce resistance and expedite land clearance for the redevelopment plan.
item.dc:creator: Nguyen Xuan Quynh

item.title: 'Real Fear' AfD Win Could Impact Investment, Says Mittelstand Chair
item.description: Christoph Ahlhaus, Chairman of the German Association of Small and Medium-Sized Businesses, tells Bloomberg there is 'real fear' the election success of the far-right Alternative for Germany in the state of Saxony-Anhalt could reduce international investment. He was speaking to Bloomberg's Oliver Crook on Daybreak Europe. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Germany's Far-Right AfD Wins State Election Landslide | Daybreak Europe 9/7/2026
item.description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.
Iran and the US carried out what appeared to be their largest tit-for-tat tanker strikes yet over the weekend, pushing oil prices higher as both nations continue to escalate a six-month war.
And speaking exclusively to Bloomberg, Jordan Bardella, head of the far-right National Rally party, set out his red lines for the battle over narrowing France’s yawning budget deficit ahead of the 2027 presidential campaign, vowing to fight any tax hike on households and business.
Today's guests: Christoph Ahlhaus, German Association of Small and Medium-Sized Businesses, Chairman; Jane Foley, Rabobank, FX Strategy Head; Marcel Fratzscher, DIW, President. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: UN Map Vote Sparks Fresh India-Pakistan Row Over Disputed Region
item.description: A United Nations resolution promoting more accurate map projections has sparked fresh tensions between India and Pakistan over a disputed territory between the two nations.
item.dc:creator: Sudhi Ranjan Sen

item.title: German Business Owners Urge Faster Reforms After AfD Victory
item.description: Germany’s small and mid-sized businesses, the so-called Mittelstand that forms the backbone of Europe’s largest economy, expressed concern about the far-right Alternative for Germany’s clear victory in a state election and urged the federal government to finally deliver on pledged reforms to revive growth.
item.dc:creator: Christoph Rauwald, Kamil Kowalcze and Mark Schroers

item.title: China Expands Patrols Off Taiwan's Pacific Coast, Raising Maritime Tensions
item.description: For decades, China’s maritime pressure on Taiwan centered on the major shipping strait separating the two neighbors. Now, Beijing is piling unprecedented pressure on its Pacific coast — a vital lifeline with US allies.
item.dc:creator: Andreo Calonzo

item.title: German Far Right Surges in State Vote in New Blow to Merz
item.description: The far-right Alternative for Germany scored its best-ever result in a state election on Sunday amid growing public discontent with the political establishment, delivering a powerful blow to Chancellor Friedrich Merz.
item.dc:creator: Kamil Kowalcze, Arne Delfs and Michael Nienaber

item.title: Bardella ‘Certain’ to Oppose Tax Hike in French Budget Fight
item.description: Jordan Bardella, head of the far-right National Rally party, set out his red lines for the battle over narrowing France’s yawning budget deficit ahead of the 2027 presidential campaign, vowing to fight any tax increases on households and business.
item.dc:creator: James Hertling and Francine Lacqua
